body.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), the kernel is bounded and continuous and is
bounded away from zero on a ball about the origin, and \(c_G\) satisfies the
stated population-Gram compatibility bound.  For every fixed
\(z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}\) and cohort \(s\),
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}]
 \le C\left\{(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}+N^{-\lambda}
 +\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right)^{2\lambda/d}\right\}.
\]
The same assertion with exponent \(\lambda\) holds after taking square
roots, and
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \Pr_{\mathbb K_\xi}(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}})\le CT^{-2}.
\]
On \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), the logarithmic
spacing term is replaced by \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  For each
\(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), these conclusions apply to its regular
conditional kernel for almost every admissible \(z_0\) under the marginal
law of the query.
body.justification: Conditional density and design mixing alone control anchor occupancy, and the repaired disintegration transfers the result to panel laws.
body.gap: The no-log conclusion requires conditional independence of design dates.
body.consumer: Marginal risk and expected length integrate the conditional anchor certificate through this bound.
